chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْه وَمُحَمَّدٌ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashi: Hamduwayh and Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: مَا فَعَلَ ابْنُ الطَّيَّارِ؟ قُلْتُ: مَاتَ. قَالَ: رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ وَلَقَاهُ نَضَرَةً وَسُرُورًا فَقَدْ كَانَ شَدِيدَ الْخِصَامِ عَنَّا أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ

translations.en: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: What happened to Ibn al-Tayyar? I said: He died. He said: May Allah have mercy on him and grant him radiance and joy, for he was an intensely vocal defender on our behalf – the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the nuanced Shia view of *khisam* (dispute), where Ibn al-Tayyar’s vigorous opposition to the Ahl al-Bayt is transformed into a merit for his eventual entry into Paradise. It underscores the principle that sincere, albeit contentious, engagement with the Imams can lead to divine mercy, reflecting the scholarly tradition of valuing intellectual struggle over mere silence.
en.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about Ibn al-Tayyar after his death?

key_terms.ابْنُ الطَّيَّارِ: Ibn al-Tayyar, a companion known for his vigorous stance regarding the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The Ahl al-Bayt (People of the House)
key_terms.شَدِيدَ الْخِصَامِ: Intensely vocal/strong in argument or defense
key_terms.نَضَرَةً: Radiance or freshness (of face/soul in afterlife)
